IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.681 OF 2026  [arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.13803 OF 2025]
ARINDAM
SEN APPELLANT  VERSUS  THE STATE OF JHARKHAND  & ANR. RESPONDENTS
ORDER 1. Leave granted.

2. By the impugned judgment and order dated 22 nd July, 2025, the High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi has disposed of the application of the appellant seeking quashing of an order dated 03rd September, 2022 by which provisional bail granted to him was cancelled by the Court of A.C.J.M.,
Ghatshila, District East Singhbhum, Jharkhand without granting relief.

entities.text: High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Appellant figures as an accused in FIR No.101 of 2018 dated 06th December, 2018 registered with Police Station Ghatshilla.

It is alleged in the FIR that the appellant has committed offence(s)
punishable under Sections 498A & 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant as well as the respondents.
5. Report under Section 173(2), Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed upon completion of investigation.
The offences are triable by a magistrate.

6. Taking an overall view of the matter, we are of the considered opinion that further detention of the appellant in custody is not required; thus, the appeal deserves acceptance and the appellant may be admitted to an order for release on bail.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order stands set aside.

8. It is directed that the appellant shall be released on bail subject to furnishing of bail bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to such terms and conditions that may be imposed by such court.

9. Needless to observe, the appellant shall not, directly or indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such facts to any police officer or to the court.
10. Appellant shall diligently attend proceedings before the trial court, unless exempted.
In case of breach, he will be liable to consequences which law provides.
11. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of bail to the appellant will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
12. The appeal is allowed on the above terms.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
